subject: SIG access controls — configuration details and artifacts
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <claire.donovan@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up — access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Monica —

Thanks for the SIG you sent last week. Our security review team had a few follow-ups specifically around access controls and evidence we need to close our review:

1) SSO / SAML: Please confirm whether SAML 2.0 is required for all users by policy (enforced at IdP level) and whether your Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) endpoints are protected by strict audience validation. If available, we also need a sample SAML metadata file or SP metadata.

2) SCIM: Does Redwood support SCIM 2.0 for provisioning and deprovisioning? Are user deprovisioning events guaranteed to result in immediate access removal in the service? Any logs/audit artifacts that show a deprovisioning event would be helpful.

3) RBAC / least privilege: We need a short description of your default role model and whether role assignment is gated by admin approval/automation. Do you offer least-privilege templates for typical roles (admin, developer, read-only)?

4) MFA: Is MFA required for all interactive accounts? What types of second factors are supported? Are service-to-service auth and API keys protected differently?

If you can send compact answers and any artifacts (metadata, access matrix, recent provisioning log extract), that should let us finish the SIG. If it's easier, we can also hop on a 20-minute call.

Thanks —
Claire
Claire Donovan
Security Engineer, Acme Corporation
sig@acme.com

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Attached are short answers and artifacts to close out the access-controls section of the SIG. See the bullets below for a concise summary; attachments include: redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf (narrative + table), sig_access_matrix.xlsx (role <-> permission matrix), and a small CSV extract of recent SCIM provisioning events.

Summary answers (high level):

- SSO / SAML:
  • We support SAML 2.0 as our recommended SSO integration. Customers may also use OIDC.
  • Enforced by policy: For enterprise workspaces (paid tier + Private/Dedicated), SAML enforcement can be enabled account-wide by admin; for hosted tier customers we recommend IdP-enforced SAML but it is configurable.
  • ACS / audience validation: Our SP validates SAML Audience, Recipient (ACS), and NotOnOrAfter timestamps. We also verify signature on the assertion using the configured IdP cert.
  • Artifact: attached file "redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf" contains an example SP metadata snippet and recommended ACS/EntityID patterns.

- SCIM (Provisioning):
  • SCIM 2.0 support: Yes. We offer SCIM for automated provisioning and deprovisioning for enterprise and Dedicated customers.
  • Deprovisioning latency: Deprovisioning requests from IdP are processed within the provisioning pipeline; in normal operation users are disabled within ~30s and full account removal/credential revocation completes within 5 minutes.
  • Audit evidence: Included small extract "scim-provisioning-logs-2026-11.csv" showing a sample deprovisioning event (user id masked) and corresponding timestamp/actor. We can produce longer ranges under NDA if required.

- RBAC & least privilege:
  • Role model: Our access model is role-based with a small set of built-in roles (Owner, Admin, Developer, Billing, ReadOnly). See attached "sig_access_matrix.xlsx" for the full permission mapping.
  • Assignment controls: Role assignment to workspace members requires an Owner or Admin action; for Dedicated/Private customers we support SCIM role mappings that can automate role assignment.
  • Templates: We provide least-privilege templates for Developer and ReadOnly which remove management/administrative permissions by default.

- MFA:
  • Requirement: MFA is required for interactive accounts on enterprise plans by default; for self-serve hosted accounts MFA is recommended and may be enforced via account policy.
  • Factors supported: TOTP (authenticator apps), WebAuthn (security keys), and SMS as a fallback (SMS usage discouraged for high-risk accounts).
  • Service/API auth: Non-interactive service-to-service access uses short-lived tokens and optional mutual TLS for Private deployments. API keys are revocable and monitored; we recommend using service principals with scoped tokens.

If you need any additional artifacts (full SAML metadata, a longer SCIM log slice, or a redacted user provisioning timeline), let me know and we can spin those up. Vivek, Rishi — tagging you for any technical clarifications or to confirm the SCIM latency statement.

Best,

Monica Patel

Monica — quick clarifying note (adding for Claire's audit):

- SCIM events: our provisioning pipeline emits both an inbound webhook event (receipt from IdP) and an internal provisioning job event after work completion. The CSV we attached contains the provisioning job events; the webhook receipt timestamp is also stored and can be correlated.
- Deprovision semantics: the initial step marks the account as disabled immediately; credential revocation (including session termination and token blacklisting) is performed in the same job and completes within the 5-minute window mentioned.
- Least-privilege: the Developer template omits the following permissions by default: workspace.billing, workspace.manage_roles, infra.admin. Customers can request custom role templates; those are tracked as change requests and require Owner approval.

If you'd like, I can produce a redacted timeline that shows receipt -> job processed -> session termination for one deprovisioning event (will need Claire to confirm redaction rules).
